title: Light Map config
description: The committed config document. Everything downstream is a pure function of it; learned data (almanacs) is not stored here. See docs/ARCHITECTURE.md (Top-level config shape) and docs/DESIGN.md (Data model).
$comment: Version 2 (P2) fixed hard_switch.source as a tagged union and added turn for presses; version 3 (P4.1) added bulb.ignored; version 4 (P5.0) fixed adaptive_config (adaptive_bulbs and the scene matrix); version 5 (P5.2a) fixed schedule_profiles (sections, triggers, collision policy) and learning; app/core/config.py migrates older versions forward. Every part of the document is validated in depth as of P5.2a. Cross-references (ids unique within their scope; members, adaptive bulbs, scene columns and schedule_profile resolve; learning units partition the adaptive bulbs; a profile's sections are the six, once each, in canonical order) are checked by app/core/config.py, not here.

version.description: Schema version. The container migrates forward on load.

rooms.description: Rooms, from HA Areas: the committed snapshot of the resolved bulb->room mapping. Every HA Area is a room.

unassigned.description: The Unassigned bucket: bulbs whose light has no HA Area. Kept in the snapshot so a bulb's id and hard switches survive while it has no room. Not a room: no switching groups, no module config.

schedule_profiles.description: Reusable time-section schedules (adaptive module). A profile with id `default` must always exist.

learning.description: Adaptive analyser tuning (P5.2a). Every field is optional; the defaults (in app/modules/adaptive/analyser.py, not written into the document) are the predecessor's and reproduce its results.

lookback_days.description: How many days of observations a nightly pass reads. Default 21.

publish_delay_days.description: A learned snapshot takes effect this many days after its newest day of data (the nightly pass, at 00:15, counts the day just begun), so a big swing can't land overnight. Ignored in bootstrap mode, so a fresh room comes alive on day two. Default 2.

bootstrap_min_days.description: Days of data before the analyser leaves bootstrap mode for learning mode. Default 7.

reactive_weight.description: A reactive event's weight relative to a heartbeat's. Default 5.

post_reactive_boost.description: The weights of the next heartbeats after a reactive event, in order. Default [3, 2, 1.5].

recency_weights.description: A day's weight by its age, first match wins; max_age_days null is the catch-all. Default 3 days: 3, 7: 2, 14: 1, older: 0.5.

confidence.description: A day's confidence band for a section, from its settled weight (or any reactive event: high), and each band's multiplier on that day's contribution. Defaults: high above 30, medium from 10, multipliers 1.5 / 1.0 / 0.5.

slug.description: Lowercase identifier, usable inside an HA object id (e.g. input_boolean.lm_soft_<id>).

entity_id.description: An HA entity id. Entity IDs only, never device IDs.

homeassistant.description: HA connection. LM_HA_BASE_URL, when set, overrides base_url; the token comes only from LM_HA_TOKEN (or LM_HA_TOKEN_FILE).

base_url.description: Used when LM_HA_BASE_URL is not set.

access_token.description: Never persisted: stripped on save and export, supplied at runtime from the environment or a secrets file.

reconnect_backoff_seconds.description: The WebSocket reconnect ladder: seconds to wait before each reconnect attempt after a drop; the last step repeats. Default [1, 2, 5, 10, 30, 60].

system.description: The observer's settings (P4). Every field is optional; app/core/config.py (system) supplies the defaults.

heartbeat_interval_minutes.description: Observation cadence, aligned to the clock: one heartbeat per room with bulbs, plus one reading per bulb, every this many minutes. Default 10.

reactive_window_seconds.description: After a room's first manual brightness change, further changes are collected for this long and recorded as one reactive event. Default 120.

reactive_min_delta.description: A bulb counts as changed in a reactive event only if its brightness moved by more than this (HA's 0-255 scale), or its power changed: filters rounding noise and transition echo. Default 5.

event_log_retention_days.description: How long the event log stays in the query layer (the Log tab). The CSV archive keeps everything. Default 90; at most a century.

data_dir.description: Where the CSV archive and the SQLite query layer live. Default, and the base of a relative path: the directory holding the config. Read at startup.

room.description: A room is an HA Area. adaptive_config is required when adaptive is true and forbidden when false.

id.description: Stable for the room's life, through Area renames.

bulb.description: One light.* entity, the actuation atom. Its soft-switch helper (input_boolean.lm_soft_<id>) and soft->bulb bridge are implicit (generated) unless it is ignored. Matched to HA by ha_match_key, or by entity_id when it has none; its id, hard switches, memberships and ignored flag travel with it when it moves or its entity_id is renamed.

ha_match_key.description: The HA entity-registry entry id of this bulb's light, recorded by the inventory. An OPAQUE match key only: the reconcile uses it to recognise the bulb when its entity_id is renamed in HA, and an Area write compares it with the registry entry at the bulb's entity_id so it never moves a different light. Never addressed, required to exist in HA, or written into generated artefacts; entity_id is what everything addresses. Absent for a light outside the entity registry, and until the first sync records it.

ignored.description: Set aside: a light.* that isn't a room bulb (an indicator or gadget LED). It stays in the snapshot, followed like any bulb so it can be un-ignored, but gets no soft switch or bridge, isn't observed or written to HA's Areas, is no switching group's or learning unit's member, and has no hard switches (app/core/config.py cross-checks these). Default false, and only ever set by the user: a new light is never ignored.

switching_group.description: A power fan-out: bulbs switched together. A named set of member bulbs plus its hard-switch bindings; it has no soft-switch entity of its own. A hard switch bound to a group acts on every member's per-bulb soft switch.

hard_switch.description: A hard-switch binding, used inside bulbs[] and switching_groups[] (not on the room). On a bulb it acts on that bulb's soft switch; on a switching group, on every member's. Generated as automation lm_hard_<id>.

mode.description: toggle: each activation turns the targets all off if any is on, else all on. press: each activation sets the targets to `turn`. follow: the targets track the source's on/off (state source only).

turn.description: press only: what each press sets the targets to. A one-way 'all off' button is a press with turn off.

hard_switch_source.description: What drives a hard switch, tagged by type: state (a stateful entity whose changes drive it), event (a stateless button firing an HA event), or device (a device automation trigger, only for a button that exposes nothing else).

state_source.description: A stateful switch, binary_sensor, light, or event.* entity. follow acts on its off->on and on->off changes; toggle and press on every real change of its state (never to or from unavailable/unknown).

event_source.description: A stateless button that fires an HA event. event_data, when given, must match a subset of the event's data, as in an HA event trigger.

device_source.description: A device automation trigger, for a button that exposes no entity or event to bind instead. The one place the config holds a device id, confined to reading a button press: it appears only in the generated trigger and never addresses a light. trigger holds the device trigger's own fields (domain, type, subtype, ...), as HA's automation editor writes them.

adaptive_config.description: Adaptive Light's per-room block (P5.0; docs/DESIGN.md, 'The adaptive editor'). Within the room each active bulb is adaptive (in adaptive_bulbs, and in exactly one learning unit) or switched-only (not listed: the plain switching plane, on at its last brightness). Every field is filled by app/core/config.py's defaults on load, and scenes is normalised there to exactly the room's units x the six sections.

lux_sensors.description: Illuminance sensors (sensor.*), averaged by the observer over those reading above 0. Existence in HA is a deploy-time check.

presence_sensors.description: Entities that read on/off for occupancy (binary_sensor.* or input_boolean.*): occupied when any is on.

schedule_profile.description: Id of an entry in schedule_profiles. Default 'default'.

adaptive_bulbs.description: Ids of the room's adaptive bulbs: active (not ignored) bulbs of this room. Adaptive-ness lives here, not on the bulb. Default empty: a room just flagged adaptive has every bulb switched-only.

learning_units.description: A free partition of exactly the room's adaptive bulbs (every adaptive bulb in exactly one unit), independent of switching groups.

scenes.description: The scene matrix: one entry per section, all six. Each holds the section's room-wide tuning knobs and a mode per learning unit.

section.description: The six fixed sections of the day, in canonical order (not necessarily chronological on a given day). app/core/config.py's SECTIONS holds the same vocabulary, so core validates the scene matrix without importing the adaptive module.

scene_section.description: One section of the scene matrix (the predecessor's scene_config, with its per-group map made per learning unit). The knobs are per section and room-wide; mode is the only per-unit setting. Learned values are not stored here.

lux_target_seed.description: A manual seed for the section's lux target, or null (the default) to OBSERVE: the lux target is learned from the heartbeats, from the first nightly pass on. Superseded by the learned target. 0 seeds nothing: a lux of 0 is a sensor's floor, a target maintenance could never reach.

lux_margin.description: The deadband either side of the target. Default 5.

max_step_pct.description: The largest single maintenance nudge, as a fraction of current brightness (0.04 is 4%). Default 0.04. Never 0: maintenance can dim a light to 1, but only a user turns one off.

maintenance_enabled.description: Whether lux maintenance runs in this section. Default false for night and sleep (lux there sits at the sensor's noise floor), true elsewhere.

units.description: Keyed by learning-unit id: exactly the room's units (normalised on load: a new unit is added as auto, a removed unit's entry dropped).

unit_scene.description: A learning unit's setting for one section.

mode.description: auto (default): learned, the unit's bulbs driven to its target. off: the unit is held off for the section (its soft switches commanded off; never a baked-in light.turn_off). Set here, by the user; the learner never decides it.

learning_unit.description: Adaptive bulbs that share one learned brightness target per section. The almanac key; its id is unique within the room and kept when it is renamed.

members.description: Bulb ids: adaptive bulbs of the room, each in no other unit.

schedule_profile.description: A reusable time-section schedule, selected by a room's adaptive_config by id (P5.2a; docs/DESIGN.md, 'Schedule profiles'). Version 5 backfilled every earlier profile with the standard schedule.

name.description: Display name, freely editable; the editor shows it beside the id.

sections.description: All six sections, once each, in canonical order (sunrise -> sleep), not necessarily the order they start in on a given day (app/core/config.py checks the order).

collision_policy.description: When computed boundaries collide (a UK midsummer sunset at 21:20 after night at 20:30, or a Nordic December where sunrise+3h overtakes sunset-3h). collapse (default): the lower-priority section is skipped for the day, honest about what happened. clamp: a section starting too soon after the last is moved to start min_section_minutes after it, keeping it alive at a time the user didn't ask for; an order inversion still collapses.

min_section_minutes.description: The shortest a section may be: one starting sooner after the last collides. Keeps a two-minute section from firing a crossover with a two-minute transition that is overridden before it finishes. At least 1 (two sections at the same instant would leave one never in force). Default 30.

profile_section.description: When one section starts each day.

name.description: A display name for the section, as the predecessor's profiles had (accepted, kept as written, and used as the boundary's name; nothing shows or sets it yet: display names, and the scene select's, are deferred past P5.2b, since the generated templates read the section id).

priority.description: Collision priority: higher wins. Default 100 for a clock trigger and 50 for a sun-relative one (a fixed time states a fact about the household's routine; a sun-relative one an assumption about daylight that a collision has already falsified), and a composite's firmest component's. Ties go to the section earlier in canonical order.

trigger.description: How a section's start is computed each day. Sun times are computed from HA's own location, so they agree with HA's sun integration.

time.description: Local wall-clock time, 24 h, in HA's time zone.

event.description: The astronomical event (not the section of that name).

offset_minutes.description: Signed, e.g. -180 for sunset minus three hours. Default 0.

oneOf.title: The earliest or latest of several
oneOf.description: 'Sunrise or 05:30, whichever is earlier'. A component that doesn't happen that day (no sunrise in a polar winter) is left out.
